chapter_name: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
learning_objective: 🎯 Learn to solve real-world puzzles involving two unknown values using graphical, substitution, and elimination methods!

main_concepts.concept_title: 📏 What is a Pair of Linear Equations?
main_concepts.simple_explanation: Two linear equations in the same two variables (like x and y) are called a pair of linear equations. The standard form is: a1x + b1y + c1 = 0 and a2x + b2y + c2 = 0.
Graphing the two lines gives three possibilities: 1. They intersect at one point (Unique solution), 2. They are parallel (No solution), 3. They overlap/coincide (Infinitely many solutions).
Without drawing graphs, you can check the type of lines by comparing ratios: a1/a2 ≠ b1/b2 (Intersecting); a1/a2 = b1/b2 ≠ c1/c2 (Parallel); a1/a2 = b1/b2 = c1/c2 (Coincident).
Find the value of one variable (say x) in terms of the other (y) from one equation, and substitute it into the second equation to solve.
Multiply the equations by suitable numbers to make the coefficients of one variable equal, then add or subtract the equations to 'eliminate' that variable.

fun_activity.title: 🍔 The Burger & Fries Puzzle
fun_activity.instructions: If 2 Burgers and 1 Fries cost ₹150, and 1 Burger and 2 Fries cost ₹120, can you write the two linear equations? (Hint: Let burger = x, fries = y). Try to solve it!

exam_tips: 📌 Always check the ratio (a1/a2, b1/b2, c1/c2) before spending time solving an equation—it might have 'No Solution'!
📌 For age-related word problems, always assume the 'Present Age' as x and y. E.g., '5 years ago' means x-5 and y-5.
📌 'Consistent' means the system has at least one solution (intersecting or coincident). 'Inconsistent' means it has no solution (parallel).
quick_recap: ⭐ The graph of a linear equation in two variables is always a straight line.
⭐ Elimination method is generally faster and less prone to fraction errors than substitution.
⭐ Word problems involving speed, distance, time, and two-digit numbers are very common in this chapter.
